name: agent-builder-roster-truthful
body: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` must name exactly the agent roster the suite supports. It must NOT offer or generate an optional `coordinator` primary agent (no roster mention, no `### coordinator (optional)` section, no "whether a coordinator is wanted" interview bullet, no primary-mode scaffold branch, no coordinator example in the register step), and it must NOT generate `implementation-phase-reviewer` (that agent is distributed by `apg init`). Its generated set is the implementers — the core/root `implementer`, per-subsystem `<name>-implementer`s, and tiered `test-implementer`s where a test tier is file-separable — PLUS an OPTIONAL per-repo `release-agent` (see `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent`), which fills the slot the removed optional `coordinator` vacated. Every generated agent is scaffolded `mode: subagent` with `hidden: true` and `generated: true`. The generated agents' push/tag grant is `ask` (human-approved) EXCEPT the `release-agent`'s, which is `allow` — that agent's push/tag is the deliberate carve-out from the recurring "push/tag remain human acts" law, and dispatching it is gated by the explicit user consent the codebase-navigator captures (see `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out`). The word "coordinator" used for the codebase-navigator's ROLE in the feedback-routing/cadence prose is retained — this law forbids only the optional generated AGENT. Satisfaction is assessed by review.
